interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is documented. Positive surgical margins is documented. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 28.44 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 22.75–34.13 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. The preoperative PSA was elevated at 25. The surgical findings included a pathological stage pT3a, positive surgical margins, and the absence of lymph node metastasis. The seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent. The biopsy revealed a higher Gleason score (4+4) compared to the prostatectomy specimen (4+3). The absence of lymph node metastasis is a favorable finding.

Countervailing factors include the positive surgical margins and the higher preoperative PSA and biopsy grade. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data significantly widens the uncertainty regarding the subsequent trajectory. The current horizon suggests a follow-up period of approximately 28.44 months without an event. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and its subsequent trend would be crucial in refining this prognosis.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT3a, positive surgical margins, and no seminal vesicle invasion. The seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent, with no lymph node metastasis documented. The preoperative PSA was 25. A key factor driving prognosis is the positive surgical margins and the higher preoperative PSA. Countervailing findings include the absence of lymph node metastasis and the absence of lymphovascular invasion. The biopsy showed a Gleason 4+4, which differs from the surgical specimen's Gleason 4+3. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up information widens the uncertainty regarding the subsequent trajectory. The prognostic horizon suggests a time to recurrence of 28.44 months. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would be crucial in refining this prognosis.
